baer-heitev/1:א: (1) to chew And it is P. Malugma, Kms. C. Tambav: And the apothecary wrote Dafilo, if it has already been chewed and placed on the back of its head before Pesach, it should be cut and removed. And it will be explained above C. Tamab Dachal that the Magma was not removed before Pesach, it is necessary to make a dala as Beit Hillel in the B. D. C. Kana who wrote Ha Dela Yelaus, we would have been during Pesach. For healing from chametz on Passover is essential' Lita Dehatam with the chametz of Akoum (and Israel is not responsible for it. And MA wrote another regulation that he would buy flour for Akoum and do the Magma according to and Farah is very doubtful about the fact that it should not be but a pill in their opinion which is evident from his actions that he does not want to accept it and here it is the opposite) A. S. Siman 27. And all this in a patient in which there is no danger, but in a patient in which there is a danger, even by Israel himself. And they put a kilo of flour and water and other markers on his sides to ease the pain if it is permissible to do so on Passover and he replied to the prohibition and concludes there indeed to do with the water of the fruits of Shafir Demi Sash:
baer-heitev/1:ב: (2) hit him But it is permissible to chew and swallow immediately. MA:
baer-heitev/1:ג: (3) Shahrukh Even a blood clot and explained in section (d) [e]] a blood clot does not miss mm AA without brushing saliva. And we were just in pacifiers. live:
baer-heitev/2:א: Nullified. This does not refer to nullification before Passover, for this was not in the category of nullification once it chametzed afterward as siman 446; rather since he gave before his animal it was nullified and he renounced it from his mind; nevertheless it is good to give them little by little so they leave none. Chafetz Chayim see there:
baer-heitev/2:ב: Saliva. Bach wrote that Mordechai also forbids only when saliva is found; so in Shach; and he challenged the Rav here since Rokeach explained explicitly only when saliva is found (and Mahari Weil) that in unspecified one must burn all remainder—this is certainly extra stringency—end. Nevertheless it appears to me specifically in a horse and the like; but in a cow that has saliva from unspecified, certainly one must destroy from unspecified; therefore give before it little by little as written:
baer-heitev/3:א: The wall. And likewise a wooden wall—Magen Avraham see there. Chafetz Chayim wrote: it appears specifically when sweating from itself or from fire heat; but if sweating from heat and steam of hot blood it is like water that makes fit for all—see there:
baer-heitev/3:ב: They forbid. Or Zarua wrote that the permitters' view is primary and Magen Avraham wrote the forbidders' view is primary; good to retain until after Passover—Chafetz Chayim. See Tur that wrote regarding dry meat sweating from water it was rinsed in—its sweat chametzs; and above siman 453 s.k. 15 from law of animal sweat:
baer-heitev/4:א: The moistened. And it implies the rest of the flour is permitted even on Passover; nevertheless afterward sift—Bach and Maharshal and Taz wrote this is mere stringency—see there:
baer-heitev/4:ב: Impossible. Such as when moistened in many places:
baer-heitev/4:ג: He should sift. The moistened place will be like dough and remain above. It appears if he need not eat from the flour on Yom Tov it is forbidden to sift on Yom Tov—see siman 507—rather sift through a gentile to destroy chametz; or give to gentile as gift before it stood mil measure—Magen Avraham. (See siman 446 and 459):
baer-heitev/4:ד: Sifting. But if he takes in hand all the moistened place it helps even if dried—Chafetz Chayim and so Taz; even during Passover he permits in such case—for only where entire sack or large part moistened then impossible to take moist place; but if possible to take moist place—it is permitted. Chafetz Chayim:
baer-heitev/4:ה: And mixes. Although flour in flour is called wet in wet and we do not say it reawakens—nevertheless crumbs are different for they do not mix well and reawaken as siman 467 seif 4; therefore forbidden to eat and permitted to retain. But if dried on Passover it is like chametz mixed on Passover—for while moist it did not mix, therefore mixed on Passover and forbidden to retain—Magen Avraham. Or Zarua wrote: where doubt whether moistened from fruit juice etc. or chametzing things—lenient to eat on Passover even if dried from double doubt perhaps fruit juice, and if you say other things perhaps nothing mixed—see there. Bach wrote: mice bit sack and ate flour and dried—before Passover sift flour, discard crumbs on sieve, flour may be retained; if found thus on Passover all forbidden for benefit. If sack unmoved without shaking, take bitten place (with some flour), tie sack there, sift, may retain, nevertheless forbidden to eat on Passover—all when visible mouse ate flour; if bit only sack and doubt perhaps ate nothing—even found on Passover may retain, forbidden to eat, even before Passover lest chametz dried and crumbles—end. Maharam of Lublin siman 119 ruled on sack bitten by mice: if baked matzot before Passover from that flour—not forbidden to eat on Passover except first two nights take other guarded flour; flour sifted from that sieve—no stringency, permitted for all—end. Taz wrote even if water fell and dried, if he recognizes moist place take it and sift rest; certainly for mouse bites take around bitten place, sift rest and eat on Passover—end. Magen Avraham wrote: in mice be more stringent, these mice are wicked and go through whole sack and eat, especially in barrel—therefore Geonim were stringent—end. So Mabit for this reason. Chafetz Chayim agreed like Taz to tie bitten place and permit rest by sifting in every case—end. Only when no moisture visible at bite; but if any moisture at bite, attribute to common thing perhaps mice urinated on flour—etc.:
baer-heitev/5:_: and milk 5.5 Milk in the crucifix even boils and is clear, and when it is congealed, it is called 3. And in the C. 177 of the Law of the fat and the text of the MA 55 the blood of the gall, the GCC does not chametz (dainah but phlegm and blood) and in that it is permissible to make a paste from it for medicine and the text of the Farah and the letter of the HH for those who have milk it does not chametz. And in human excrement, it worsens in siman 19. And it is simple that the columnist and the author wrote here Damhamitsin.

machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (s.k. 1) Not so, etc.—implies permitted, etc.—for otherwise since only teaching saliva chametzs:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (And in s.k. following) If so should teach briefly forbidden chew and swallow and we know human saliva chametzs; nevertheless such is permitted:
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (s.k. 2) And place, etc.—and see YD end 255 we hold like Rambam: not in manner of enjoyment permitted for illness without danger; therefore Rambam challenged mishnah shall not chew and place on wound—therefore brought Kesef Mishneh:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: Therefore must be, etc.—transgresses bal yera'eh—not benefit prohibition for not in manner of enjoyment. See Tosafot beginning 29: if Jew chews even gentile chametz—liable for responsibility even intending rob via chewing. Even intending steal via chewing liable:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ד: Because difficulty, etc.—from where Talmud intended mishnah teach incidentally healing virtues of wheat for wound; perhaps law itself forbids placing on wound for benefit—but per Magen Avraham no benefit prohibition here not in manner of enjoyment. See 453:6 law wants existence. Why Pri Chadash forbids even gentile chametz—Jew wants chametz existence; therefore fruit juice—see his words:
machatzit-hashekel/3:א: (s.k. 3) Since, etc.—book of rabbanan—perhaps no saliva in them:
machatzit-hashekel/3:ב: And even if you say, etc.—still Rama's words not settled—for he wrote since already nullified—implies unspecified nullified on eve; Magen Avraham intent for law: even if nullifies now before giving to animal—not effective as 448—even hefker animal forbidden chametz; though Magen Avraham 445:2 permits throw chametz to hefker pig though fear eats—here like gave before animal though not yet chametzed:
machatzit-hashekel/4:_: (Sk. D) The sweat of the wall, as in the Psalms and Asi' of the NT. R. Lafuki from Ma'an Degras, the sweat of the donkey is sustainable.
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: (s.k. 5) And some say—requires study—for contrary Rav's custom one view primary; here contrary 'some forbid' should be primary:
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: (2) And the Rashi disagreed. Ral Dharukah wrote Dziyat Homa ab dela mikiri mishka for the matter of kosher regarding impurity. MM for the matter of mimuz mikri mishka domiya druk adam which I do not prepare and af yes misses. And the Rash difficult why compare sweat to saliva In other words, like brown sweat for human sweat. And just like the sweat of a person, the Omnipresent does not miss the sweat of the wall. And since the Rash made it difficult for him to see MM, we did not find that he had a share in the law on him, as in the 3rd chapter of siman 19. which he received while connected. Even on the back of a damboar above C. 177 Even on the back of a dakl grapes rain fell on them when they were connected and also to scorch two shebels ras tsg aaag rains fell on them in a connected APA they changed when they were swallowed by grapes or branches and were called fruit water and Tsel Deetz I:
machatzit-hashekel/6:_: (s.k. 6) Take in hand—even so sift afterward. Taz wrote only stringency to sift:
magen-avraham/1:א: (1) Not to chew, etc. It means that a person who chews and swallows immediately misses out:
magen-avraham/1:ב: Place on wound. Rambam chapter 5 Foundations Torah: not healed with prohibitions in manner of enjoyment—worms, chametz on Passover; but not in manner of enjoyment—poultice, melogma from chametz or orlah, bitter drinks with forbidden food—no palate enjoyment—permitted for ill—end; see YD 255. Kesef Mishneh: Orchot Chayim on Rambam permits melogma from gentile chametz loaned or placed on wound without Jewish responsibility; if no melogma for gentile Jew buys flour gentile makes melogma—end. Therefore shall not chew—specifically Jewish chametz—bal yera'eh; see Tosafot beginning 29; perhaps therefore Ketubot 83 'words of sages heal'—why teach place on wound—for prohibition bal yera'eh not benefit—not in manner of enjoyment—came teach incidentally wheat good for wound; Yerushalmi refutes 24 Shabbos: dangerous poultice chametz on Passover—implies without danger forbidden; there permitted Jew himself though bal yera'eh; Hagahot Maimonides 14 from Magen Avraham: remedy must be known—see there very stringent; see 453:6:
magen-avraham/2:_: Since already nullified. Then rabbinic doubt; requires study—for not on eve only all chametz but this chametzed now not in nullification as 446; even if before giving says all remnants nullified—must burn lest animal return and eat as 448—therefore custom Mahari Weil/Maharil give little by little so none remains:
magen-avraham/3:ב: And some forbid. Requires study—for contrary most forbid—Rokeach; Rosh did not dispute practically; Ramaz writes unspecified chametzs; Rivash; Tur words—only in Hagahot Maimonides chapter 5 permits; appears forbidders' reason: wall sweats from water within as 462:6 dry meat—and wooden wall may have absorbed water while attached:
magen-avraham/4:א: Take in hand. Even so afterward sift (Bach, Maharshal):
magen-avraham/4:ב: And if impossible. Such as moistened on side in many places:
magen-avraham/4:ג: Sift flour. Moist place like dough remains above; if need not eat flour on Yom Tov forbidden sift on Yom Tov (507)—sift through gentile to destroy chametz; though sifting Torah melacha here no waste—not father melacha; if wishes give gentile gift before mil measure (467, 458:2):
magen-avraham/4:ד: For it crumbles and mixes. Although flour in flour nullified in sixty—visible crumbs reawaken as 467:4—forbidden eat, permitted retain (and see EH 104, Beit Yosef 115). If dried on Passover like chametz mixed on Passover—for while moist did not mix, mixed on Passover—forbidden retain as Rav's son-in-law reason. Bach: mice ate flour—if dried before Passover sift and keep after Passover; found on Passover all forbidden benefit; sack unmoved—take bite place, tie, sift all sack, may retain, forbidden eat Passover—all when mouse ate flour; bit only sack doubt ate nothing—even Passover may retain, forbidden eat, even before Passover lest chametz dried crumbles—end. I explained all this in responsum. Maharam Lublin 119 on mouse-bitten sacks sifted—pressure: take other guarded flour first two nights, bake matzot from bitten flour before Passover; sifted flour from that sieve—no stringency, all permitted—end. Taz: even water fell and dried, if recognizes moist place take and sift rest; certainly mouse bites around bite, sift rest, eat Passover—end. Mice be more stringent—wicked mice through sack, especially barrel—Geonim stringent—end:
magen-avraham/5:_: The dew etc. The excrement of chickens is not fermented (Tor) and because of an animal (pharmacist) and the above-mentioned conversion fees, it is not fermented that is discolored like blood and putrid phlegm, and it is permissible to make a paste from it for medicine:
mechaber/1:main: If the saliva and foot water and the like are missed. And in it there are six sections: A person should not chew on teeth and put on top of it because they miss the saliva misses:
mechaber/2:main: (2) One who gives barley to his animal and finds saliva (3) among them must burn them: {Rama: But from unspecified need not concern since already nullified (logical opinion}; and some are stringent to burn all the animal's remainder even if no visible saliva on it: (Mordechai beginning chapter Elu Overin in name of Rokeach)}
mechaber/3:main: (3) A sack full of flour that became moist from (6) the wall's (7) sweat (4) is permitted; (8) and some forbid:
mechaber/4:main: (9) Water fell on flour (10) or the sack became moist; (5) he should take in his hand all (11) the moist place in the sack until he washes (12) all flour in the sack; (13) and if impossible to do so (6) (2) he should sift the flour (14) and the rest is permitted—but only while moist; if the moisture (15) dried, (16) sifting (17) does not help for it crumbles (18) and mixes with the rest (19) and it is forbidden to eat it (20) on Passover (21) rather he should sift and guard until after Passover (22) and if it dried on Passover (23) it is forbidden to retain it:
mechaber/5:main: The dew misses as well as the water of the feet and the water of the mouth and the nose and the eye and the ear (but blood) (R. Yeruham) and milk and a person's sweat does not miss (Tor):
mechaber/6:main: Flour that has been spilled all day long does not come to be chametzed, and it is that the spilled is tored without interruption, and we will bake it immediately when it stops, and if it is supplied, if the leaked is tored, or not, it is forbidden:
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) And place on wound, etc.—through chewing in mouth wheat mixes with saliva and chametzs when on wound mil measure—transgress bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei; even chewed and placed before Passover remove when sixth hour eve unless spoiled unusable for dog as 442. Poskim: all this Jewish wheat; gentile wheat gentile chews and lends Jew to place on Passover—permitted if no Jewish responsibility on poultice—for gentile poultice no bal yera'eh; if gentile has no wheat Jew may buy flour for gentile, gentile chews, Jew receives as loan only. Though chametz forbidden benefit even gentile chametz as 443—here different: benefits from chametz not in manner of enjoyment—only rabbinic prohibition; illness even without danger they did not decree; nevertheless if can heal by softening wheat poultice with fruit juice—not proper through saliva:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) (b) Because they are sour - and 27 if he is struck by it, there is no danger in it, but when there is a danger in it, it is permissible even in a place where there is no dbi, if only it is possible that this medicine will benefit him and it is not easy to do otherwise, and even eating and drinking a finished form of chametz Nami is permissible for his treatment, since there is a danger in it:
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (1) (c) It is necessary to pile up - Druk makhmutz and so on and so on, it is necessary to pile up even if the animal did not stop to eat it for about a thousand mm.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (4) Since already nullified—then out of d'oraisa concern—for even certainly chametz no longer Torah destruction only rabbinic; therefore when unclear saliva we do not establish prohibition—Acharonim wondered what helps nullifying all chametz on eve for chametz chametzed now on Passover; wrote wording garbled—intent if explicitly nullified before giving animal and said all barley animal leaves I nullify—end:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (5) Even without visible saliva, etc.—for unspecified they have saliva; Acharonim wrote all this in horse etc.; but ox and cow certainly stringent even from unspecified—known they expel saliva when eating as 324:17; good stringent all animals burn remainder even without visible saliva; therefore l'chatchila give little by little so none remains from eating:
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (6) The wall—and likewise wooden wall that sweats:
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (2) (g) It is permissible - there is no difference whether the sweat comes from a lack of air as is found in basements and caves where the walls and stones sweat, or whether it comes from the presence of water in it, such as in a new brick wall that sometimes sweats because the walls have not yet dried or in a wooden wall where the trees are moist and sweat in all shades. And it's not better than fruit water, and so according to what they wrote above in the sign of the 17th, fruit dams with water are in a hurry to ferment, you shouldn't knead them to begin with, and if it's still soaked, we'll dance and the soaked will last until the end of the day, and what's left will be kneaded and baked for Pesach. The sack for the history of water and misses:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (3) And there are some who forbid - Salah Dela Yalpinan sour cream from kosher is impure, and as for sour cream, any wetness of water has the power to make sour, and some have written this opinion per the fact that the wall sweats from the strength of the water it has, and even the sweat of a wall of wood is also judged as water, because according to most it has the ability to be swallowed by rainwater that drips on the walls and sometimes rainwater drips on them after they have been cut from the ground And according to this taste in the sweat of stones or metals or glass, even this sabra does not miss and like the fruits of my blood. And the main point of view is as the first opinion and as the author just stated in the beginning and which fruits they are and how much it should be felt for the beginning in the opinion of the osrin and however for the suspension after Pesach sheri and if you want to use this flour for Pesach you must permit it by dancing and even if it dries up and the dirty flour will be thrown away and the rest will use it:
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (10) Or sack became moist—from water; per 'some forbid' previous seif—even from wall sweat. Since sack moistened, moisture presumably reached flour there:
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (11) Moist place—with flour there; take flour with sack around moisture per estimate somewhat more:
mishnah-berurah/4:ד: (12) All flour in sack—l'chatchila afterward sift all remaining flour; some wrote only if moisture on bottom of sack this remedy taking from moist to sack edge helps; if water from above on sack—how does taking from above help—perhaps water penetrated deep like water enters depth below and perhaps dried there—cannot recognize moist place—therefore no leniency without sifting even b'dieved; perhaps before Passover not stringent b'dieved without sifting:
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (13) If impossible—moistened many places, or large part of sack, or threw sack place to place—presumably flour mixed inside:
mishnah-berurah/4:ו: (14) Rest permitted—where moist flour sticks like dough remains above sieve; flour through sieve holes certainly untouched by water; if Yom Tov forbidden sift more than need—sift through gentile to destroy chametz; if water fell Yom Tov and water not in flour mil measure yet—gift to gentile before chametzed:
mishnah-berurah/4:ז: (15) Sifting does not help—even before Passover. Acharonim: specifically sifting not help when dried—but first remedy take moist place helps even dried on Passover if sack not moved and moist place recognizable well as above—rest permitted eat, nevertheless good sift remainder:
mishnah-berurah/4:ח: (16) For it crumbles, etc.—fine crumbs descend through sieve holes mix with flour; though certainly sixty against them nullified before Passover—on Passover days forbidden smallest amount reawakens; though wet in wet we do not say reawakens as 467:4 and flour in flour is wet in wet—crumbs do not blend well, exist independently—perhaps even at dough kneading not dissolved—on Passover days reawaken and forbid:
mishnah-berurah/4:ט: (17) Forbidden to eat, etc.—even if baked before Passover—for crumb baked is chametz not nullified as above. See Pri Chadash holds wet in wet does not reawaken—still many Acharonim agree after baking one lump nullified does not reawaken; see Magen Alef wrote further take some flour eat before Passover and hang prohibition on what ate—may rely in loss; nevertheless take other matzot first nights—for not guarded properly—likewise wherever we permit from double doubt:
mishnah-berurah/4:י: (18) On Passover—and mice bit sacks: if visible ate flour and moisture dried—some say if on Passover all forbidden—for we attribute mice went many places—mouse saliva chametzs like other animals—therefore taking that place not help; before Passover sift and retain or sell as water-moist law. Many Acharonim hold also here taking around bite with flour helps, sift rest, eat Passover—even on Passover; nevertheless good stringent first view except pressure/loss; all when sack unmoved flour not mixed; if shook sack or many bites impossible take and sift—no remedy even lenient view—law like water moistening. Per end previous s.k. even sack moist from water in loss may bake before Passover—here likewise. See Shaarei Teshuvah on this:
mishnah-berurah/4:ל: (20) If dried on Passover, etc.—we hold chametz mixed on Passover in smallest amount; if not mixed in time gives taste—if dried on Passover though moisture before Passover—all while moist did not mix—when began mix when dried and crumbled into flour—mixture on Passover in smallest amount—forbidden retain—even if sifted fear small crumbs through sieve holes as above. Unlike dried before Passover—we hold gives taste in all flour, here no such measure. Acharonim: whole seif when known moistened from water; if doubt fruit juice—lenient eat on Passover by sifting even dried on Passover—double doubt perhaps fruit juice, if chametzing things perhaps nothing mixed from dried moisture; nevertheless if easy find other flour for Passover—l'chatchila do not rely double doubt eat—hide until after Passover; likewise if moistened something disputed fruit juice or water—permit by sifting:
mishnah-berurah/4:מ: (21) Forbidden to retain—not wrote throw out—for he goes to 467:10; per him may sell to gentile except prohibition value; per Rama custom there burn all—here likewise. Per many Acharonim in great loss may rely Mechaber 467:3 and sell whole sack to gentile except small chametzed flour—plain gentile dish before him:
mishnah-berurah/5:א: (1) The dew, etc. - all of which are demachmitsin, i.e. if he was idle, a rate of acidification without a grain of water due to occupation does not come to acidification:
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (23) And likewise urine—human adult or minor; but animal and other creatures—dispute whether chametzs:
mishnah-berurah/5:ג: (24) And water of mouth, nose, etc.—human or other creatures—for all are offspring of water and are like water:
mishnah-berurah/5:ד: (4) (so) but blood - and the the Master is the blood of bile because there is no sourness that has turned like blood and putrid phlegm and so it is permissible to make a paste from it for medicine:
mishnah-berurah/5:ה: (5) And milk - in the Kmetz and the 15th milk in Zyriy [as well as fat] if it is boiling and clear and the 4th is congealed and the taste in the 27th is nothing but like fruit water and there are no chametzs and AAG dahlab and blood in the 10th are forbidden mm void in the 60th mashak chametz in Pesach which is in something:
mishnah-berurah/5:ו: (6) And the sweat of a man - and the sweat of an animal, refer above to the symbol of the NT 77 and the MB there. And excrement between Dadam and Deshaar in the Gemara is not missed, and therefore if we wet a bag of flour with excrement from the flour and the dough that is there, we will throw it outside and the rest is permitted. And indeed in feces, but in the water that comes out of the anus, and also in feces that are very soft. The arbitrators wrote that the dhats that are found because of the animal, even if they are softened, are not acidified by the moisture that is there, the flagellum does not miss, and so on:
mishnah-berurah/5:ז: (7) (KH) does not miss - here they are all equal to the one who does not miss when he is alone, but there is a difference between them.
mishnah-berurah/6:א: (1) (x9) It doesn't come, etc. - that the leaker is prevented from missing the flour soaked in the leaked water, and even if the moisture spreads further from the place where the leak occurred, it hits there mmm due to the irritation of the leaker, who hits with force and swallows drop by drop, he does not allow everything around him to miss:
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (30) Drip must be continuous, etc.—drops fall consecutively all day—otherwise waits between drops combine to mil measure as 459:2 gloss; some Acharonim explain: when not consecutive drops cannot prevent chametzing:
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (31) And bake immediately when it stops—do not leave moist flour without occupation—knead and bake immediately as 459:2; l'chatchila; b'dieved forbidden only if waited mil measure after drip stopped:
mishnah-berurah/6:ד: (4) (heart) and if it is provided - despica dauriita is and even its stay is prohibited. And the the Master knows in the grain of the Omnipresent's din that the leak plagues him one after another, even the whole day, it does not come to be pickled, and if it does not come down one after another, it will be oxidized by the water, and even when it comes down one after another, immediately the comma has to be ground:
mishnah-berurah/6:ה: (33) Forbidden—see Pri Megadim tends forbid all moist flour—for we are not expert what counts drop after drop—see there:
turei-zahav/2:_: And there are stricters. We were the apothecary who said that a cow with its saliva should burn what is left so that it does not miss Akal, which means that there is no saliva in front of us.
turei-zahav/3:_: permitted. Dziaia is similar to human sweat which does not ferment and this is the opinion of the Rabbi and Yesh Osrin is the pharmacist who dimmed the sweat of the wall to the saliva that ferments and in section 5 the Rama brings that human sweat does not ferment:
turei-zahav/4:א: Take in hand, etc.—implies rest of flour permitted even on Passover; Maharshal wrote must afterward sift as written after:
turei-zahav/4:ב: (2) Not fun to dance. Meaning, but the first correction, that is, he who holds in his hand the moistened place is mehni Efi' in the dry, since he takes all the place where there is doubt, what do we have any more fear and in Mordechai P. 27 20, a case came before the Rari of Vienna about a sack of flour that fell into the mortar on Passover, he ordered to empty the sack and said that the flour should be managed so that the saucer remains on top and it is thrown away, and the rest is allowed in that 20 and precisely 27 that it is moistened, but if the sack stood until If we wash the bowl, it is not fun to manage a dumpling and go in with the rest and not leave anything on top, and we need to take another flour for the purpose of Passover, and we will manage it if it is found to be like mush, we will throw it away, and the rest will be kept until after Passover, and precisely if we are dry before Passover, then we can keep it until after Passover, etc. But on Passover, they will throw everything away. Here, there is no mention here of the rule of adding a percentage instead of the wet, and we were because it was not possible, since the entire sack or a large part of it fell into the mortar and there is no Taqqel, but by dancing in this, he said, "Della Mahni, when we dry, lest it crumble and come down with the flour through the holes of the sifter, but by fixing it, which will take the place of the moisture and take the rest, why would it not be useful even to dry it later? It is permissible even without dancing, even though the late Mo'ah, in the name of Rashel, also on this repair, held the place of the moisture, the SMM should manage all the rest of the construction, as well as the custom of Akal. And evidence from the Mash in Tor, if a little water or snow falls on the grain, the upper one will rake and the lower one will take it, and here in the grain there is no dance, but surely dancing Dankt Rashal is nothing but hardware, since it is possible for the most slavish worker, but not forbidden without dancing, after that, in the drying up and an imaginary dance After he had taken all that the Omnipresent had in him and I did not say, Dasur Delma fell from the dry land to Mt. through the Napa and Amash C. NTNG 33 from canceling flour with flour: And if mice ate flour with flour, he will take 300 grams of that place and surround it well and the rest we will manage and eat on Passover without a grain of water that fell on flour in place A and this does not seem to make it worse if we make on Passover the law of water that fell on flour It is Meiri Efi' in Pesach as the main part of the laws. Even though the late Mu'ah overstated the measure in S. of the NT that is not as Mash: another 20 the column in the name of the RA from Germizaa a bag with flour and roosters sitting in it and their moscha will be moistened does not miss who will dance the flour and throw the dough outside and the rest is permissible Akal: and an additional apothecary AZ Amri' in the offerings of a page of Set Barleys The ones that were found because of an animal, like an animal, were sacrificed at your expense, and it is not forbidden because of chametz akal, and above, simply Dmhat said here, Dirkd and will throw it out, like a dachion damtza is a mitzvah, and since the rest of the matzahs are for the purpose of the 19th, it is not appropriate to practice zion in them. And if it happened that they did not dance the flour, there is no prohibition here at all:
turei-zahav/6:_: And if doubtful, etc.—Beit Yosef in name of Ran: Rosh wrote not continuous drip forbidden—even what we do not see soaked in water—for flour absorbs moisture and law as soaked—end; if continuous drip permitted others not soaked—Ran concludes unclear. Appears he disputes both: continuous drip permits even soaked—as Rosh and Tur bake immediately; if not continuous drip forbidden only that place—not this absorption concern:
